# iliad-134 — new renderings (21.200–297)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ποταμὸς βαθυδίνης (21.212, 21.228; as subject, with προσέφη) | "the river, deep-eddying" | "the deep-eddying river" | "the deep river", "the whirlpool river"; follows the shipped βαθυδίνης "deep-eddying" (iliad-133, 21.143) |
| ἀνέρι εἰσάμενος (21.213) | "having made himself like a man" | "taking the likeness of a man" | "disguised as", "in the form of"; follows the table's εἰσάμενος "taking the likeness of" (13.45) |
| ἀϊδήλως (κτείνεις ἀϊδήλως, 21.220; sense not certain) | "destructively" | "destructively" (+ note: ancient gloss "making unseen, annihilating") | "ruthlessly", "unseen", "cruelly", "mercilessly" (each decides the open question) |
| ἄγη μ’ ἔχει (21.221; ἄγη "amazement", the ancients also "distress") | "amazement holds me" | "amazement holds me" | "I am dismayed", "I am distressed", "wonder"; not ἄγη "breaks" (ἄγνυμι, 3.367) |
| ἔσται ταῦτα Σκάμανδρε διοτρεφές, ὡς σὺ κελεύεις (21.223) | "These things will be, Scamander, Zeus-nurtured, as you bid." | "It shall be so, Zeus-nurtured Scamander, as you command." | "Be it so", "Very well"; διοτρεφές "Zeus-nurtured" as in the table (διοτρεφές, 10.266; 9.229), Σκάμανδρος as the Latinised form shipped at 5.773 |
| ὑπερφιάλους ἐναρίζων (21.224) | "the overweening ones, despoiling them" | "killing and stripping the overweening Trojans" | "slaying" (kept for ἐνήρατο, ἔπεφνε), "plundering"; ἐναρίζω "strip a slain man of his arms", as in the table (5.155) |
| ἐρίβωλον ἄρουραν (21.232) | "the rich-clodded plough-land" | "the rich-soiled plough-land" | "fertile fields", "the rich earth"; ἐρίβωλος "rich-clodded" / "rich-soiled" as in the table (9.329), ἄρουρα "plough-land" with the hyphen, as the table has it (3.115, 4.174) |
| δείελος ὀψὲ δύων (21.231–232) | "evening, setting late" | "evening … setting late" | "late dusk", "the evening of the day"; ὀψέ "late" |
| ἦ, καὶ … (21.233; the river’s speech closed, “he” = the river) | "He spoke, and" | "So he said, and" | "So he spoke" (reserved for ὣς φάτο); the table's ἦ καί (1.219), unchanged |
| κυκώμενος (21.235), κυκώμενον κῦμα (21.240) | "churning" · "churning" | "churning" · "churning" | "stirred up", "roiling", "foaming"; κυκάω "churn" |
| ὤθει δ’ ἐν σάκεϊ πίπτων ῥόος (21.241) | "the flood, falling on his shield, thrust him" | "the flood, falling on his shield, pushed at him" | "struck", "beat on", "hammered"; ὠθέω is `l` "thrust", `i` "push", as in the table (2.744) |
| ἀκροκελαινιόων (21.249; rare, from ἄκρος + κελαινός) | "blackening at the surface" | "darkening at the surface" (+ note: formation, not usage, gives the sense) | "black-crested", "dark-topped", "blackening at the tip"; the note does not decide whether it is the crest of the swell or the whole surface |
| ὅσον τ’ ἐπὶ δουρὸς ἐρωή (21.251) | "as far as the rush of a spear reaches" | "as far as the rush of a spear reaches" | "flight" (listed as avoided for ἐρωή, 4.542), "a spear's cast", "a spear-throw away"; ἐρωή "rush" |
| αἰετοῦ οἴματ’ ἔχων μέλανος τοῦ θηρητῆρος (21.252) | "with the rush of an eagle, the black one, the hunter" | "with the rush of the black eagle, the hunter" | "the swoop of", "the dark hunting eagle"; οἶμα "rush", as in the table (16.752); the same English word now renders ἐρωή in the line before, each fixed by its own house row |
| ὅς θ’ ἅμα κάρτιστός τε καὶ ὤκιστος πετεηνῶν (21.253) | "which is at once the strongest and the swiftest of winged things" | "which is at once the strongest and the swiftest of winged creatures" | "mightiest" (ἴφθιμος), "fleetest"; κάρτιστος "strongest" as in the table (1.266–267) |
| σμερδαλέον κονάβιζεν (21.255) | "terribly rang" | "rang terribly" | "dreadfully" (δεινόν "fearsomely"), "fearsomely", "awfully", "clanged"; κοναβίζω "ring" as in the table (2.466) |
| ἀμάρης ἐξ ἔχματα βάλλων (21.259; ἔχμα rare) | "casting the obstructions out of the ditch" | "casting the obstructions out of the ditch" | "dams", "stones", "clods", "stoppers" (each decides what blocks the channel), "supports" (the table’s ἔχματα, 13.139, a departure: there the word is the supports of a rock, here what holds up the water in a ditch, and “supports” makes no sense of it); ἔχμα "thing that holds" |
| ὀχετηγός (21.257) | "channel-leader" | "a man who leads the water-channel" | "irrigator" (anachronistic ring), "ditcher", "gardener"; ὀχετός "channel" + ἄγω "lead" |
| ἡγεμονεύῃ (ὕδατι ῥόον, 21.258) | "guides the flow with water" | "guides a flow of water" | "leads the stream", "directs the water"; the table's ἡγεμών "leader" |
| ὀχλεῦνται (21.261) | "are heaved up" | "are heaved up" | "are rolled", "are shaken", "are jostled"; ὀχλέω "heave" |
| κελαρύζει (21.261) | "gurgles" | "gurgles" | "murmurs", "babbles", "purls"; κελαρύζω |
| λαιψηρὸν ἐόντα (21.264) | "quick" | "quick" | "nimble", "swift" (θοός, ὠκύς); follows the table's λαιψηρός "quick" (10.358) |
| θεοὶ δέ τε φέρτεροι ἀνδρῶν (21.264) | "for the gods are stronger than men" | "for the gods are stronger than men" | "greater", "better" (ἀμείνων); φέρτερος "stronger" (2.201) |
| πλάζ’ ὤμους καθύπερθεν (21.269) | "beat on the shoulders from above" | "beat upon his shoulders from above" | "struck", "buffeted", "drove back"; πλάζω "drive back" kept apart from πλάζομαι "wander" |
| ὑπέρεπτε (κονίην … ποδοῖιν, 21.271; hapax) | "was gnawing away" | "gnawing the dust from under his feet" | "undermined", "washed away", "ate away"; from ὑπό + ἔρεπτομαι "feed on" (21.204), the note says so |
| ᾤμωξεν ἰδὼν εἰς οὐρανὸν εὐρύν (21.272) | "cried out, looking to the wide heaven" | "cried out, looking up at the wide heaven" | "groaned" (στενάχω), "wailed"; ᾤμωξεν "cried out" (13.198), οὐρανὸν εὐρύν "wide heaven" |
| Ζεῦ πάτερ ὡς οὔ τίς με θεῶν ἐλεεινὸν ὑπέστη (21.273) | "how none of the gods undertook, pitiable as I am, to save me" | "how none of the gods has undertaken to save me, pitiable as I am" | "if only", "would that"; ὡς "how", ὑφίσταμαι "undertake" (4.267) |
| ἔπειτα δὲ καί τι πάθοιμι (21.274) | "and then let me suffer even something" | "and after that, let me suffer whatever may come" | "afterward let me die", "even if I suffer"; the optative is not decided in the note |
| Οὐρανιώνων (21.275) | "the sons of Uranus" | "the sons of Uranus" | "the Uranians", "the gods of heaven" (the Odyssey's), "the Titans"; follows the Iliad's own row (5.898) |
| ψεύδεσσιν ἔθελγεν (21.276) | "with lies charmed" | "beguiled me with lies" | "deceived", "bewitched"; θέλγω "charm" |
| λαιψηροῖς … βελέεσσιν (21.278) | "quick shafts" | "quick shafts" | "swift shafts" (ὠκύς), "nimble"; follows the table's λαιψηρός "quick" and βέλεσσι "shafts" |
| ἐνθάδε γ’ ἔτραφ’ ἄριστος (21.279) | "was raised here the best" | "the best man raised here" | "bred", "born and reared"; τρέφω |
| ἐρχθέντ’ … ὡς παῖδα συφορβόν (21.282) | "shut in … like a boy, a swineherd" | "shut in … like a swineherd’s boy" | "hemmed in" (kept for εἴλω, 1.409), "caught", "trapped"; ἔργω "shut in" (16.481); συφορβός "swineherd" (21.189) |
| ἔναυλος (21.283) | "a torrent" | "a torrent" | "a gully", "a flash flood", "a ravine"; the note does not choose between "watercourse" and "gully" |
| ἐπιστώσαντ’ ἐπέεσσι (21.286) | "they pledged him with words" | "they made their pledge to him in words" | "reassured", "swore", "gave pledges"; ἐπιστόω "make sure, pledge" |
| χειρὶ δὲ χεῖρα λαβόντες (21.286) | "taking him hand by hand" | "clasping his hand" | "taking him by the hand"; the Greek is "taking hand with hand" |
| μήτ’ ἄρ τι λίην τρέε μήτέ τι τάρβει (21.288) | "neither tremble at all too much, nor be afraid" | "do not tremble overmuch, nor be afraid" | "do not fear too greatly" (merges τρέω and ταρβέω); τρέω "tremble", ταρβέω "be afraid" |
| τοίω … ἐπιταρρόθω (21.289, dual) | "such helpers … we two" | "we two are such helpers for you" | "helpers at hand", "champions"; follows the table's ἐπιτάρροθος "helper" (5.808, 24.182), the dual shown by "we two" |
| ὡς οὔ τοι ποταμῷ γε δαμήμεναι αἴσιμόν ἐστιν (21.291) | "so it is not fitting for you to be overcome by a river" | "so it is not fitting for you to be overcome by a river" | "it is not your fate", "it is not destined"; αἴσιμος "fitting" (7.310) |
| πυκινῶς ὑποθησόμεθ’ (21.293) | "we will suggest to you shrewdly" | "we will make shrewd suggestions to you" | "counsel", "advise" (listed as avoided for ὑποτίθημι, 8.36), "solidly" (the table's πυκινός "solid" is for things), "wisely", "closely"; ὑποτίθημι "suggest", πυκινῶς of counsel is "shrewd" |
| μὴ πρὶν παύειν χεῖρας … πρὶν … ἐέλσαι (21.294–295) | "not to stop your hands … before … you have hemmed in" | "do not stop your hands … until you have hemmed in the Trojan army" | "penned" (avoided for εἴλω, 1.409), "check your hands"; infinitive as command; ὁμοίϊος "common to all" (9.440, 13.358) |
| δίδομεν δέ τοι εὖχος ἀρέσθαι (21.297) | "we give you to win a boast" | "and we grant you to win the triumph" | "glory" (κῦδος); `l` "boast" and `i` "the triumph", as in the table (εὖχος, 22.7) |

Departures from the Odyssey: none.

Departures from the house table: ἔχματα "obstructions" at 21.259, against the table’s "supports" (13.139); see the ἀμάρης ἐξ ἔχματα row. No other.
